strengths: The paper addresses a practically important constraint: unlearning using only the trained model and labeled forgetting data. The target-versus-irrelevant logit sensitivity objective is simple and offers a useful refinement over uniform sensitivity suppression.

Class and subclass results are promising. MU-Mis achieves average accuracy gaps from retraining of 0.07 on CIFAR-100 and 0.20 on CIFAR-20-Sea, substantially improving over several remaining-data-free baselines.
Reported efficiency gains are substantial against SalUn: 83 versus 2630 seconds on Tiny ImageNet with ResNet-18, and 3 versus 81 minutes with ViT.

The evaluation includes six datasets, multiple architectures, five-trial main comparisons, sequential deletion, and loss-component ablations. The implementation link and experimental details support reproducibility.
weaknesses: The central theoretical connection is not established. Section 3.2 drops training-trajectory and softmax derivative terms and assumes the aggregate cross-sample residual is negligible. Appendix D's ReLU argument does not justify this assumption, particularly for correlated samples. Sensitivity to perturbing a training input also does not establish its deletion influence. Additionally, Eq. (A7) omits the softmax curvature term and is incorrect even for linear logits.

The broad utility-preservation claims exceed the evidence. In Table A8, MU-Mis achieves retained/test accuracies of 70.48/57.37, versus 100/84.45 for retraining and 100/84.41 for RUM. Table A16 shows substantial failures on highly memorized samples. Even Table A7 does not consistently favor MU-Mis over other remaining-data-free methods. These are significant limitations for sample-level deletion and should qualify the abstract and conclusion.

Practical parameter selection without retained data remains unresolved. Stopping thresholds vary from 0.68 to 3.00 across tasks and reach 10 in sequential deletion; selected experiments additionally use an 80-fold loss reweighting. Figure A2 examines only one task over thresholds 0.7–1.0. A transferable selection protocol and ablations of the reweighting are needed to substantiate easy deployment and robust stopping.

The privacy conclusions are stronger than the auditing supports. A lower fraction of forgotten samples classified as members does not by itself establish retraining equivalence or resistance to membership inference. SCRUB-LiRA provides useful additional evidence, but attack calibration, shadow-model construction, and negative-sample selection are insufficiently documented. Matched baseline evaluations and attack performance at low false-positive rates would strengthen the privacy assessment.

Implementation and reporting discrepancies require clarification. Appendix F.4 fixes the irrelevant class to 1 for random-subset experiments, whereas Algorithm 1 requires a randomly selected class different from the true label; handling label-1 samples is unclear. Table A1 omits random-subset hyperparameters. Tables A7 and A11 also report unexplained entropy-MIA values of 33.04 and 83.34 for MU-Mis under the CIFAR-10 10% deletion setting.
